title: Dynamic-programming value
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols, let $x$ be a Boolean string, and let $s,V$ be natural numbers. Define $D(t,c)$ for natural numbers $t,c$ recursively: at $t=0$, it is $1$ if the encoding of $x,c,s$ belongs to the machine’s accepting language and $0$ otherwise. At time $t+1$, sum over all $c'<V$ the value $D(t,c')$ once for each of the two fixed-choice machines whose transition relation takes encoded value $c$ to $c'$ within the specified bound.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols
caveat: The payload omits definitions of the accepting language, transition relation, encoding, and fixed-choice step, so their precise semantics cannot be fully stated.
